title: No-op ternary `color: isUsed ? accentColor : accentColor`
description: Inside the chip button's inline `style` object, the `color` property is computed as `isUsed ? accentColor : accentColor`. Both branches of the ternary yield the identical value (`accentColor`), so the conditional is dead code. It can be simplified to `color: accentColor`. The distinction between used and unused chips is already carried entirely by `background`, `border`, `opacity`, and `cursor` on the surrounding lines, so the text colour is intentionally constant — the ternary just obscures that.
evidence: style={{ background: isUsed ? withAlpha(accentColor,0.08) : withAlpha(accentColor,0.12), border: `1px solid ${isUsed ? withAlpha(accentColor,0.2) : withAlpha(accentColor,0.35)}`, color: isUsed ? accentColor : accentColor, opacity: isUsed ? 0.5 : 1, cursor: isUsed ? "default" : "pointer" }} — the `color` line evaluates to `accentColor` regardless of `isUsed`.
behavior_preservation: Identical rendered output: both branches already produce `accentColor`. No test asserts the colour value (CategoricalValuePicker.test.tsx only checks opacity and onAddValue behaviour), so replacing with `color: accentColor` is purely cosmetic in the source.
